case_name: Bharat Singh v Management of New Delhi Tuberculosis Centre
respondent:
Management of New Delhi Tuberculosis Centre
Supreme Court of India

4 April 1986
Civil Appeal No. 1251 of 1986
The Judgment was delivered by : V. Khalid, J.
Special leave granted.

It was directed that the commencement of the Act would be on such date as the Central Government may, by a Notification in the Official Gazette, appoint. facts: Section 17-B was inserted in the Industrial Disputes Act by the Industrial Disputes (Amendment) Act, 1982 (Act 46 of 1982).
The Central Government appointed the 21st day of August, 1984, as the date on which the Act would come into force.
The Delhi High Court held that Section 17-B applied only to awards that were passed subsequent to the coming into force of this Section, namely 21st August, 1984.
The appellant joined the Management of New Delhi Tuberculosis Centre, Jawaharlal Nehru Marg, New Delhi, as a Peon against a permanent regular post.
He was promoted as a Daftry and his services were terminated by a Memorandum dated September 13, 1975.
The Labour Court directed that the appellant would be entitled to back wages with effect from 19th May, 1979 only, at the rate at which he was drawing them when his services were terminated.
On January 31, 1984, the Management moved the Delhi High Court, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India challenging the award and applied for stay of the operation of the award.
issues: Whether Section 17-B applies to awards passed prior to 21st day of August, 1984?
petitioner_arguments: Section 17-B mandates the Court to award full wages if the conditions in that Section are satisfied.
The legislature was aware that because of the long pendency of disputes in Tribunals and Courts, on account of the dilatory tactics adopted by the employer, workmen had suffered.
respondent_arguments: Section 17-B has application only to cases where the awards were passed after the commencement of Section 17-B; in other words, after August 21, 1984.
The respondents' contention is that a Section which imposes an obligation for the first time, cannot be made retrospective.
court_reasoning: It is only when the award is challenged and the challenge is pending, that the Section becomes operative.

If this is the object, then would it be in keeping with this object and consistent with the progressive social philosophy of our laws to deny to the workmen the benefits of this Section simply because the award was passed, for example just a day before the Section came into force?
A rigid interpretation of this Section as is attempted by the learned counsel for the respondents would be rendering the workman worse off after the coming into force of this Section.
holding: The Court held that Section 17-B applies to awards passed prior to 21st day of August, 1984.
The Court directed that the employer shall be liable to pay such workman, during the period of pendency of such proceedings in the High Court or the Supreme Court, full wages last drawn by him.
